a multivariate modeling framework should be adopted to model injury counts of different road-user types, while accounting for spatial dependence effects.

the spatial multivariate count models provide a better fit to the data than the spatial univariate models, and that the models that accommodate spatial dependence in the counts of both road user types outperform the models that accommodate the spatial dependence in the pedestrian or bicyclist count only.
the spatial multivariate count models are more effective at modeling pedestrian and bicycle crashes by injury severity than the spatial univariate models.

we developed and applied a spatial multivariate count regression model that can accommodate spatial dependence effects and can be used for the analysis of bicycle and pedestrian injury counts by severity level.
